message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on a 3D-printed topographical model of a city. Candidate headings are 9023 (instruments, apparatus and models designed for demonstrational purposes, unsuitable for other uses), 4911 (printed matter), 9021, and 3926.

Heading 9023.00.00 covers models designed for demonstrational purposes. A topographical relief model used for informational or architectural display fits this heading. Heading 9023 is the better fit than 9013 or 3926. Heading 9023.00.00 has subdivisions: 9023.00.0000 is the only one at the 8-digit level. Its statistical suffix would be 9023.00.0000.

Heading 9023 would exclude 4905 (maps, including relief maps), but 4905 covers relief maps and globes, so it needs consideration. Heading 4905 covers "Maps and hydrographic or similar charts of all kinds, including atlases, wall maps, topographical plans and globes, printed." Relief maps are included in the 4905 scope per the Explanatory Notes, covering "relief maps or globes" whether or not in relief. The 4905.99 provision covers other items, and 4905.91 covers in book form. A 3D-printed city model with a wooden frame is a relief model of a city, so 4905.99.0000 is plausible. Because the item is "printed" in a loose sense, yet its material is plastic from 3D printing, it is not really printed matter. CBP has ruled that 3D-printed topographical models are classified in 9023.00.0000 as demonstration models. I'll go with 9023.
